stories.title: Indian startup funding rises to $290 million
stories.summary: Indian startups raised $290.55 million between November 2 and November 7, a 69 percent increase from the previous week. GIVA led the activity with a $100 million round, accounting for nearly 34 percent of the total capital. Three rounds accounted for 75 percent of the week's funding.

stories.title: Green SM invests in Indian electric vehicle operations
stories.summary: Vietnam-based electric mobility company Green SM has invested Rs 152.65 crore in its Indian subsidiary through a rights issue. This follows an Rs 85 crore investment in June 2026, bringing the total capital infusion to approximately Rs 238 crore for expanding electric vehicle operations in India.

stories.title: Unify Foodworks raises seed funding for restaurant expansion
stories.summary: Unify Foodworks has raised Rs 5 crore in seed funding to expand the presence of Moe’s Casa Mexicana and Carvel across the National Capital Region. The master franchisee plans to increase store density and strengthen consumer recall as it works toward building national restaurant chains.

stories.title: Bucketlistt.com raises seed funding for travel expansion
stories.summary: Travel-tech startup Bucketlistt.com has raised Rs 7.6 crore in a seed round led by Kairon Capital. The Ahmedabad-based company operates a marketplace for curated travel experiences and plans to use the capital to expand its network into new destinations including Manali and Bir.

stories.title: Fashion discovery app Slayd raises pre-seed funding
stories.summary: Gurugram-based Slayd has raised $156,400 in pre-seed funding to expand its team and private-label apparel business. The platform uses automated indexing to aggregate inventory from over 300 brands into discovery feeds for its reported 200,000 users. The company plans to recruit across engineering and product teams.

stories.title: Froncort.AI secures funding from Google.org
stories.summary: Healthcare AI startup Froncort.AI has received $2.3 million from Google.org to scale its disease surveillance platform. The package includes cloud credits and technical expertise to develop mAI-NETRA, a mobile tool that uses satellite imagery and health data to identify infectious disease risks for frontline health workers.

stories.title: Israeli AI security startup Bay raises $50 million
stories.summary: Israeli startup Bay has raised $50 million in funding after less than a year of operation. The company says it addresses a primary barrier to AI adoption by allowing autonomous agents to perform work safely while enterprises retain control. Customers include Micron, Peloton, ClickUp and Wix.

stories.title: Lumbra raises $25 million for defense-focused AI agents
stories.summary: DC-based AI startup Lumbra has announced a $25 million Series A to scale its agent operating system. The company focuses on the defense and national security space, claiming its agents can do more than manage calendars. It now plans to expand into regulated commercial sectors.

stories.title: Daylight raises $80 million Series B
stories.summary: Israeli cybersecurity company Daylight has raised $80 million in a Series B round led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives. The company combines AI agents with human security experts to detect and respond to threats. It reports that revenue has grown more than 40-fold over the past year.

stories.title: SoftBank reports gains from Lenskart and Meesho
stories.summary: SoftBank Vision funds recorded gains of nearly $400 million from Lenskart and Meesho during the September quarter. Lenskart contributed $273 million in returns, while Meesho added $121 million. The investor identified these as two of the strongest performers in its global listed portfolio.

stories.title: SoftBank books valuation loss on Ola Electric
stories.summary: SoftBank Vision Fund 2 reported a $42 million valuation loss on its investment in Ola Electric for the quarter ended September 2026. Gross returns from the EV maker fell to $370 million, down from $412 million in the previous quarter. The fund has invested $556 million total.

stories.title: Redalpine closes eighth fund at $250 million
stories.summary: Swiss venture capital firm Redalpine closed its eighth fund at $250 million, reaching its hard cap in under 12 months. The new fund is 25 percent larger than its 2024 predecessor. This closing occurs despite an overall decline in fundraising activity across German-speaking countries.

stories.title: Proximal Ventures raises $27.5 million for AI drug discovery
stories.summary: Sahir Raoof has raised $27.5 million for his debut fund, Proximal Ventures. The firm aims to back startups using AI to transform drug development infrastructure and services. The fund enters the market during what is described as one of the toughest fundraising environments for first-time managers.

stories.title: Baylor College of Medicine launches biotech fund
stories.summary: Baylor College of Medicine has unveiled the BCM Legacy Fund I to invest in early-stage biotech startups. Funded by philanthropies, the vehicle has already backed Nemea Therapeutics, a spinout developing an oral drug for metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. The investment amount was not disclosed.

stories.title: MakeMyTrip India arm receives IPO approval
stories.summary: MakeMyTrip India has received approval from SEBI to launch an initial public offering. The company filed draft papers confidentially in July 2026. The offering is expected to consist entirely of an offer for sale by existing shareholders, potentially raising over $1 billion for the travel aggregator.

stories.title: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings files for IPO
stories.summary: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings has filed draft papers for an initial public offering. The issue will be an offer for sale of up to 99.75 crore shares by the promoter. Because the offering is entirely an offer for sale, the company will receive no proceeds from the listing.

stories.title: ShareChat parent reports wider losses
stories.summary: Mohalla Tech, parent of ShareChat and Moj, reported a 79 percent increase in net loss to 1,978 crore rupees for the 2026 fiscal year. Operating revenue rose 40 percent to 1,016 crore rupees. Management claims the company recorded its first EBITDA positive quarter in Q1 FY27.

stories.title: Matrimony profit rises in September quarter
stories.summary: Matrimony reported a 165 percent increase in net profit to 20.7 crore rupees for the September quarter. Operating revenue grew 18 percent to 134.8 crore rupees, driven primarily by the matchmaking business. Total expenses for the quarter rose 2 percent compared to the same period last year.

stories.title: ShareChat’s FY26 Snapshot, MakeMyTrip’s IPO & More
stories.summary: Inside ShareChat’s Mixed FY26 ShareChat parent Mohalla Tech delivered some hits and some misses in FY26. While the homegrown social media giant crossed the ₹1,000 Cr revenue mark and found a new growth engine in microdramas, what played the spoilsport were losses and surging expenses.

stories.title: Anthropic targets $1 trillion valuation for IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic is targeting a valuation of up to $1.02 trillion for its upcoming IPO. The company aims to raise as much as $64.4 billion, with shares priced between $70 and $78. The offering serves as a test of investor appetite for the AI sector.

stories.title: Anthropic retracts IPO filing details
stories.summary: Anthropic sent and then retracted details regarding a potential $69.3 billion IPO. The initial filing suggested a share price range of $70 to $80, but the company informed bankers the figures were inaccurate. Investors have discussed valuations ranging from $1.1 trillion to $1.3 trillion.

stories.title: Sarvam appoints former Google Cloud India MD as president
stories.summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam has appointed former Google Cloud India Managing Director Sashikumar Sreedharan as its president and chief business officer. Sreedharan will oversee enterprise operations, marketing, and finance while joining the company board. He brings 35 years of industry experience to the role.

stories.title: OpenAI introduces Control Room to stop rogue AI agents
stories.summary: OpenAI has unveiled Control Room, a safety feature designed to halt artificial intelligence output that raises security concerns within 35 seconds. The tool connects research inference workloads with misalignment monitoring systems. The company says the feature is critical as model risks become bigger.

stories.title: Founders using AI for patents face legal risks
stories.summary: Startups are increasingly using AI to research and draft patent applications to save money. While these tools can generate documents in minutes, they often miss the legal and strategic nuances required for commercial value. AI capabilities remain jagged when applied to complex intellectual property law.

stories.title: Gramiyaa faces high costs on quick commerce platforms
stories.summary: Premium edible oil brand Gramiyaa entered quick commerce via Blinkit in 2024, only to find itself paying nearly twice the commission of national competitors. The company discovered that listing on platforms is not the end of the battle, but the beginning of managing razor-thin margins.

stories.title: Forest Essentials grew from a kitchen setup to a major brand
stories.summary: Luxury Ayurvedic brand Forest Essentials began in 2000 with a 2 lakh rupee investment and two employees. Founder Mira Kulkarni, a single mother, grew the business from a small kitchen setup into a company now valued at 500 crore rupees. Success arrived after a modest start.

stories.title: Mumbai businessman finds success in strawberry farming
stories.summary: Ketan Sodha, a 57-year-old entrepreneur with no farming background, has built a soilless strawberry farm in Mahabaleshwar. His venture, Berry Fresh Agrotech, manages 19,500 plants and has generated 44 lakh rupees in sales. He transitioned into agriculture after a career in land dealing.

stories.title: Chirag Munjani builds tourism startup around rural experiences
stories.summary: Chirag Munjani founded Rural Pleasure Journeys to focus on experiential travel rather than traditional luxury vacations. The Vadodara-based startup works directly with local artisans and received an award for cultural immersion in 2017. The business prioritizes local engagement over standard hotel packages.

stories.title: Bout India finds success by avoiding standard travel packages
stories.summary: Founded in 2013, Bout India built its business by refusing to sell fixed itineraries. Managing Director Himanshu Maru focused on personalized travel plans to differentiate the company from competitors. The firm has since earned over 970 reviews from its global clientele.

stories.title: Storytelling as a competitive advantage for startups
stories.summary: At TechSparks 2026, Shweta Rajpal Kohli of the Startup Policy Forum argued that storytelling is essential for startups to differentiate themselves. As competitors gain access to similar capital and talent, founders must use authentic narratives to build trust and explain their unique value.

research.title: AVCORP: Identifying and Resisting Deception via Communication Theory and Theory of Mind
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Today's LLM-based agents are vulnerable to deception by users and other agents. Defending against deception requires Theory of Mind (ToM) reasoning to infer the beliefs and goals of others as well as modeling tactics based on. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: AYO: A Safe and Privacy-Preserving Platform for Studying Children's Interaction with LLMs
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Children and adolescents are increasingly interacting with generative AI and large language models (LLMs), yet little is known about how these interactions may influence their development, beliefs, and behavior. Existing research has relied heavily on surveys. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Adversarial Evaluation of Large Language Models for Patient-Friendly Radiology Report Summarization
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Purpose: To develop and validate a scalable adversarial evaluation framework for assessing the robustness of large language models (LLMs) that generate patient-friendly summaries of radiology reports. Methods: We introduced a clinically grounded adversarial framework that uses. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: AutoEMatic: Runtime-Adaptive Mixed-Precision LLM Inference via Automatic Exponent-Mantissa Refinement
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing LLM post-training quantization techniques determine precision before inference begins, yet the precision a model requires varies dynamically across prompts, layers, and inference phases. We present AutoEMatic, a full-stack co-design that adapts the precision of weights. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: CoRA-Bench: Evaluating Evidence Preservation by Context Selectors Under Token Budgets
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Context selection can reduce input length during long-input inference but can remove evidence required to answer a query. We introduce CoRA-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating evidence preservation under shared token budgets. We compare head and tail. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Conformal Fair Decoding for Large Language Model Recommenders
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate personalized recommendations without task-specific training, but changing a protected attribute while holding interaction history fixed can alter the semantic content of recommended items. We study fairness control when model weights. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: DeepResearch RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models for Deep Research Report
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Empowered by Large Language Models (LLMs), deep research systems integrate online information into research reports through multi-step web searching and information synthesis. Evaluating these reports presents a significant challenge due to their long context, high information. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Do large language models rank moral values? A transitivity test of moral competence
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs are increasingly used to support decisions that require moral consideration. While LLMs perform well on morality benchmarks from psychology and philosophy, producing appropriate outputs on these benchmarks (moral performance) does not establish that an LLM. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
